question: The equivalent weight of phosphoric acid (H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>) in the reaction NaOH + H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> → NaH<sub>2</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O is:
explanation: Only one replaceable hydrogen is neutralized per molecule of H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> to form NaH<sub>2</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>. Therefore, n-factor = 1, and Equivalent weight = 98 / 1 = 98.

question: What volume of CO<sub>2</sub> is obtained at STP by heating 10 g of 90% pure limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>)?
explanation: Pure CaCO<sub>3</sub> = 90% of 10 g = 9 g. Moles = 9 / 100 = 0.09 mol. CaCO<sub>3</sub> → CaO + CO<sub>2</sub>. Moles of CO<sub>2</sub> = 0.09 mol. Volume at STP = 0.09 × 22.4 = 2.016 L.

question: Which of the following solutions has the highest normality?
explanation: Normality = Molarity × n-factor. For 1 M H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>, n-factor = 3, so Normality = 3 N (highest among the choices).
